title: Room-temperature superconductivity in a carbonaceous sulfur hydride

original_source.note: Full author manuscript, methods and extended-data captions read from OSTI; publication identity and retraction checked against Nature.

source_manifest.title: Retraction Note: Room-temperature superconductivity in a carbonaceous sulfur hydride
source_manifest.finding: Nature retracted the paper over data processing and analysis. The notice identifies undocumented, nonstandard magnetic-background subtraction and loss of confidence in susceptibility data; the authors disagreed. Retraction does not independently establish that every materials result is false.

source_manifest.title: High-Temperature Superconductivity in Hydrides: Experimental Evidence and Details
source_manifest.finding: Eremets and colleagues explicitly report significant unsuccessful efforts to reproduce C–S–H room-temperature superconductivity. They distinguish this from independently reproduced H3S and LaH10 superconductivity.

source_manifest.title: Missing theoretical evidence for conventional room-temperature superconductivity in low-enthalpy structures of carbonaceous sulfur hydrides
source_manifest.finding: Gubler and colleagues searched over 17,000 structures and studied 3,000 promising candidates. Their conventional-superconductivity calculations did not explain the reported room-temperature result; they retain unsearched structures or unconventional physics as possibilities.

source_manifest.title: Structure and composition of C-S-H compounds up to 143 GPa
source_manifest.finding: Bykova and colleagues tested the original synthesis and a methane-based variant, measured structures and Raman spectra, and directly compared original Raman data. They could not reproduce the proposed methane incorporation from elemental carbon; their resulting materials differed from the original report. They did not measure the central room-temperature superconducting result.

source_manifest.title: Enhanced superconductivity in C-S-H compounds at high pressure
source_manifest.finding: Liao and colleagues used the original 1:1 carbon:sulfur composition as a specific starting point for independent first-principles searches, predicting C2S2H4 and C2S3H4 with transition temperatures far below room temperature.

source_manifest.title: Superconducting ternary hydrides: progress and challenges
source_manifest.finding: Zhao and colleagues explicitly say the withdrawn Snider paper sparked a series of high-pressure C–S–H studies. They distinguish antecedent 2020 predictions from subsequent research and report unresolved composition and later calculated transition temperatures below room temperature. Online publication was December 2023; issue date July 2024.

source_manifest.title: Observation of Conventional Near Room Temperature Superconductivity in Carbonaceous Sulfur Hydride
source_manifest.finding: Pasan and colleagues claim 260 K superconductivity at 133 GPa from susceptibility and optical measurements. Multiple original authors, including Dias and Salamat, are present; this is not independent replication and predates the three-year anniversary.

source_manifest.title: Retraction: Carbon content drives high temperature superconductivity in a carbonaceous sulfur hydride below 100 GPa
source_manifest.finding: Authors retract a same-team 2022 extension because they lost confidence in origins of electrical transport measurements. They explicitly maintain the X-ray crystallography and structure calculations, while superconductivity conclusions become uncertain.

source_manifest.title: Carbonaceous sulfur hydride system: the strong-coupled room-temperature superconductor with a low value of Ginzburg-Landau parameter
source_manifest.finding: Wrona and colleagues defend compatibility with a strong-coupling superconducting interpretation. Their model takes the experimental 287.7 K temperature as input and estimates thermodynamic parameters; this is affirmative theoretical interpretation, not independently collected experimental support.

source_manifest.title: Dilute carbon in H3S under pressure
source_manifest.finding: Wang, Zurek and colleagues investigate specific carbon-doped structural candidates motivated by the report. They identify local bonding changes and limits of rigid-band approaches, without experimentally establishing the original superconducting state. Some authors collaborated with the original team in separate structural work; not used as the sole independent-group evidence.

answers.rationale: Independent theoretical work offers a favorable conditional interpretation, but takes the reported transition temperature as an input. Independent experimental efforts failed. The rubric does not specify whether such conditional model support qualifies as support of the central experimental claim; it is not treated as experimental validation.

search_gaps: Conditional theoretical support and successful independent experimental support are not equivalent; claim_supported lacks a rule for this distinction.

Uptake questions can record useful substantive scrutiny without validating the central claim; enabled_new_result and external_utility do not specify whether research motivated by a failed claim qualifies.
No confirmed independent operational adoption or successful room-temperature transfer found; these absences remain unknown.
Late positive validation, substantive post-October-2023 use, and surviving comparative utility were not established. Later search results largely repeated the earlier controversy.
Some publisher pages restricted full text. Original manuscript was obtained in full from OSTI. Source scopes explicitly identify abstract-only or relevant-section reads.
Lifetime observation through 2026-09-16; this selected landmark challenge case is not an unbiased training sample.
research.summary: The room-temperature claim was retracted and a documented independent replication effort failed. Independent teams nevertheless tested the synthesis, compared spectra, and extended C–S–H structural calculations; a later review explicitly attributes a research stimulus to the paper. Affirmative conditional theory and same-team follow-ups do not establish independent experimental validity. Utility and durability remain incompletely evidenced rather than automatically negative.
